meta.blurb: In Oshenar, even a spoonful of water is counted, and Ysra Vell counts better than anyone. When the Deep Well starts to fall and her father rides away, she follows him across the Glass Desert. Someone is stealing the river.
meta.bible: Ysra Vell: sixteen, daughter of a water merchant in Oshenar, sharp with numbers, honest, stubborn, learns to read the desert. Dorin Vell: her father, a kind water merchant who believes that water is a promise. Rhodric Stane: the Guildmaster of the Well-Guild, polished and greedy, who steals the river. Teyo: nineteen, a Sandwright wind-reader and guide, funny, calm, never in a hurry. Granny Orla: an old water-seller who gives Ysra a map. Pebble: Ysra's patient strider, a long-legged desert riding beast. Oshenar: the city built around the Deep Well. Deep Well: the city's only well, with a rope marked in hands. Silver Vein: the ancient underground river that feeds the well. Glass Desert: the wide desert north of the city, where storms fuse sand into glass. Dry Sea: the old name for the sand plain. Stone Gate: an old gate in a cliff, where the Silver Vein is held back by a sluice. Channelwrights: the old engineers who built the channels and painted murals. Sandwrights: the desert travellers who read wind and share water by law. Well-Guild: the guild that runs the city's water. Open Well Law: the new law of fair, shared water. Brass Cup: the Vell family's measuring cup, which becomes the city's measure. Dew-sail: a cloth that gathers dew. Glass storm: a hot storm that throws glassy sand. Sunrise Gate: the city's east gate. Cold Springs: the northern springs Dorin goes to check. Voice and tone: clear, warm and tense; desert survival told with true, simple science (dew, shade, aquifers, evaporation); the villain is greed, nobody dies, and the ending is hopeful. Pell: a seven-year-old neighbour girl with a chipped clay cup, who asks big questions. Maro: the baker next door, loud and kind, who keeps the shop key. Bastian: the caravan driver who comes back alone, sunburnt and ashamed. Fennick Dray: Stane's thin agent in a grey coat, who smiles coldly and speaks softly. Mother Sabe: the old keeper of a hidden Sandwright rock pool. Captain Harl: the commander of the Guild guards at the Stone Gate, tired and honest underneath. Elder Maris Thorne: the oldest member of the Well-Council, fair and slow to speak. Amma Zeri: Teyo's grandmother, who taught him that the desert is a book. Lantern Star: the one bright star that never moves, which travellers steer by. Old Cistern: the old stone water tank outside the east wall where the Sandwright camp stands. Rope Keeper: the old man at the Well-House who reads the marked rope. Well-House: the stone building over the Deep Well. Well-Council: the twelve elders who judge the city's laws. Guild Hall: the Well-Guild's marble building in the high district. Spyglass: Teyo's small brass looking-tube, the only thing of value he owns. Three hands: the rope's marks are counted in hands, and a fall of three hands is a great fall. The Brass Cup has been polished by three generations of Vell hands. Science kept true: dew forms when a cold cloth cools the air around it; a mirage is hot air bending light; sand grows cold fast at night; glass storms are fiction, in which lightning fuses sand into glassy grains. Nobody dies in this book. Strider: the long-legged desert riding beast of this world. Dew-sail: a fine cloth stretched low to catch dew. Channelwrights built a vast Stone Gate in the eastern cliffs. The Cold Springs lie in the north, reached by an old road that winds east beneath the cliffs. Law of Scarcity: the law Stane wants Dorin to sign, handing the city's water to the Guild for ever. Skiff: a long flat sail-driven sled on iron runners that glides over hard ground, used by the Guild. Bronze door: a low green-black door beside the Stone Gate, the entrance to the Channelwrights' tunnel. Tobin: a broad, grey-bearded winch-man at the Stone Gate camp with four children in Oshenar, who first refuses Stane's order. Tally Book: Captain Harl's honest blue-covered record of every barrel the camp filled.

beats.scene: A girl fills clay jars on a rooftop as dawn lights a shining city
beats.summary: At dawn in Oshenar, Ysra Vell fills water jars on her rooftop above a city built round one well.

beats.scene: Flat roofs and blue tiles stretch toward a round stone well-house
beats.summary: From the roof Ysra sees the whole of Oshenar, every street running inward to the Well-House and the Deep Well.

beats.scene: A girl counts stairs and jars on a narrow staircase
beats.summary: Ysra has always counted everything, because numbers are the one thing in the desert that never change their mind.

beats.scene: Dorin opens wooden shutters and hangs a polished brass cup by the door
beats.summary: Her father Dorin opens the family shop and hangs the old brass cup that measures every sale.

beats.scene: A baker with flour on his eyebrows holds out a jug to be filled
beats.summary: Maro the baker buys three cups of water, and Dorin measures it to the brim, never a drop more or less.

beats.scene: Dorin smiles over the brass cup while Ysra writes in a ledger
beats.summary: Dorin tells Ysra that water is a promise, and a promise must stay the same size for rich and poor.

beats.scene: A small girl holds up a chipped clay cup at the counter
beats.summary: Little Pell from next door comes for her morning cup, and Ysra fills it and answers her question about the desert.

beats.scene: A busy market with striped awnings and blue banners over every stall
beats.summary: At noon Ysra crosses the market, where the blue banners of the Well-Guild hang above every stall.

beats.scene: A long silent queue winds past a dyer's shop toward the well-house
beats.summary: Whispers say that the Deep Well is falling, and the queue at the Well-House is longer than ever.

beats.scene: Ysra and her father lean over the well and look at a marked rope
beats.summary: At dusk the Rope Keeper shows them that the water is three hands lower than a month ago, the lowest ever.

beats.scene: A crowd fills the market square as a bell rings from a tall tower
beats.summary: The next morning the Guild Hall bell rings, and all of Oshenar gathers in the square to hear the Guildmaster.

beats.scene: A man in blue silk robes and silver rings climbs onto a draped platform
beats.summary: Rhodric Stane, the Guildmaster, mounts the platform: smooth, polished and wearing silver rings.

beats.scene: Stane spreads his hands before a hushed and worried crowd
beats.summary: Stane tells the city that the Deep Well is failing, and that every citizen must make sacrifices.

beats.scene: A woman covers her mouth as the crowd gasps in the square
beats.summary: Stane announces that from tomorrow the price of water will double.

beats.scene: Guards in blue coats form a line before an angry crowd
beats.summary: The crowd shouts, but guards step forward, and Stane says nobody can blame the Guild for the weather.

beats.scene: Dorin hangs the brass cup on its hook and looks at it
beats.summary: Back at the shop, Dorin refuses to double his price, and Ysra works out what it will cost them.

beats.scene: Ysra frowns over a ledger by the light of a single lamp
beats.summary: Ysra's figures do not fit: the well has fallen three hands in a month though the city drinks no more than usual.

beats.scene: An old seamstress holds out a jug and a few coppers
beats.summary: An old woman cannot afford the Guild's price, and Dorin fills her jug at the old price.

beats.scene: Ysra puts one eye to a gap in a high wall
beats.summary: Delivering jars in the high district, Ysra spies Stane's green garden of palms and fountains.

beats.scene: Heavy carts loaded with barrels creep out of a garden gate in the moonlight
beats.summary: At night three carts of full barrels leave Stane's garden, lanterns covered, for the eastern gate.

beats.scene: Ysra bursts through the shop door while her father rises from his chair
beats.summary: Ysra runs home and tells Dorin about the garden and the secret carts; he goes to an old chest.

beats.scene: An old cracked map spread on a counter shows a thin silver line
beats.summary: Dorin unrolls a map so old its edges are soft, with a thin silver line drawn far below the desert.

beats.scene: Dorin traces the silver line with one finger while Ysra leans close
beats.summary: Dorin explains the Silver Vein: a hidden river that creeps through deep sand and rock and fills the Deep Well.

beats.scene: Stone channels run across a faded map toward a tiny blue city
beats.summary: The Channelwrights dug channels to guide the Vein and built a vast Stone Gate in the eastern cliffs.

beats.scene: Dorin points at the northern edge of the map by lamplight
beats.summary: If the Vein is blocked the well will empty, so Dorin must go to the Cold Springs and see for himself.

beats.scene: Father and daughter argue across a table by a flickering lamp
beats.summary: Ysra begs to come, but Dorin says she is the one person he trusts to keep the shop and the promise.

beats.scene: Drivers load water skins onto tall striders in a busy yard
beats.summary: Dorin gathers a small caravan with Bastian and another driver, four striders and enough water for a fortnight.

beats.scene: Dorin hugs Ysra at a gate in the grey light before sunrise
beats.summary: At the Sunrise Gate Dorin gives Ysra the brass cup and tells her not to follow him if he is late.

beats.scene: A line of tall riding beasts leaves the city gate at sunrise
beats.summary: The caravan leaves at sunrise, and Ysra watches until the dust settles.

beats.scene: Ysra chalks a mark on the wall of an empty shop
beats.summary: Ysra opens the shop alone for the first time and chalks the first day on the wall.

beats.scene: Chalk tally marks multiply on a shop wall beside a warm loaf
beats.summary: Day after day Ysra opens the shop and marks the wall, while Maro brings a warm loaf each morning.

beats.scene: Ysra frowns over a ledger beside empty barrels
beats.summary: The Guild charges the shop double for every barrel, yet Ysra keeps her father's price.

beats.scene: A small girl carries a full cup carefully across a street
beats.summary: On the eighth day Pell asks whether Ysra's father is back, and Ysra says soon.

beats.scene: A girl stands alone at a city gate as the sun sets
beats.summary: On the tenth day Ysra waits at the Sunrise Gate until the guards send her home.

beats.scene: A tally of chalk lines covers a wall beside a dark window
beats.summary: Twelve days pass, then fifteen, and still the eastern road is empty.

beats.scene: A sunburnt man collapses in the dust before a kneeling girl
beats.summary: On the fifteenth evening Bastian limps back alone, and Ysra gives him water from the brass cup.

beats.scene: Bastian weeps in the dust beside a girl with a brass cup
beats.summary: Bastian tells how armed men stopped the caravan on the eastern road and took Dorin.

beats.scene: A girl climbs marble steps toward a tall doorway
beats.summary: At the Guild Hall a clerk writes down her name but asks no questions.

beats.scene: A thin man in a grey coat leans over a shop counter
beats.summary: Fennick Dray offers to buy the Vell shop cheaply, and Ysra refuses.

beats.scene: Ysra sits among empty jars with the brass cup in her lap
beats.summary: Ysra pours her last jar among her neighbours and decides to find her father herself.

beats.scene: A caravan master shakes his head at a girl in a busy yard
beats.summary: Ysra asks every caravan master in Oshenar for a guide, and every one refuses.

beats.scene: An old woman sells water from a clay jar beside a nearly dry fountain
beats.summary: Granny Orla, the oldest water-seller, sees Ysra's tired face and puts down her ladle.

beats.scene: An old woman kneels to pull a flat wooden box from under a bed
beats.summary: Orla listens to the whole story and leads Ysra into her back room.

beats.scene: A hand-drawn map on thin leather with a silver thread running across it
beats.summary: Orla gives Ysra a hand-drawn map of the Silver Vein, copied by her grandmother from the Channelwrights.

beats.scene: Orla holds a girl's chin and speaks seriously by a window
beats.summary: Orla warns Ysra about storms, false lakes and moving dunes in the Glass Desert.

beats.scene: An old woman points toward a distant wall and a stone water tank
beats.summary: The Sandwrights camp at the Old Cistern, and Orla says to look for a young man who whistles.

beats.scene: A woman offers a cup of water outside grey tents beside a stone tank
beats.summary: Ysra walks out to the Sandwright camp, where a woman gives her water without being asked.

beats.scene: A young man in a blue robe watches a ribbon fluttering on a pole
beats.summary: Ysra meets Teyo, a wind-reader, who teases her for walking like someone chased by numbers.

beats.scene: Ysra spreads a map on the sand and holds it down with four stones
beats.summary: Teyo laughs at her request until he sees Orla's map and the silver thread.

beats.scene: A girl and a young man shake hands over a map in the sand
beats.summary: Teyo refuses her coins but agrees to guide her for her father's finest dew-sail.

beats.scene: Ysra lifts a grey veil-like cloth from an old chest
beats.summary: Ysra takes Dorin's finest dew-sail from the chest under the stairs.

beats.scene: A tall pale strider lowers her head to be scratched in a stable
beats.summary: Pebble, the family's old strider, is tall, slow and calm, and she seems to know the plan.

beats.scene: Teyo lays a row of empty water skins across a shop floor
beats.summary: Teyo explains that two skins a day for ten days will be needed, and that the skins will be filled outside.

beats.scene: Ysra covers a page with figures while Teyo reads an old map
beats.summary: Ysra works out how far their water will last, and Teyo says she can count a desert.

beats.scene: A big baker holds a bag of flat bread beside a shop door
beats.summary: Ysra gives Maro the shop key, and he gives her bread and keeps her secret.

beats.scene: Two figures lead a tall strider through dark streets under a thin moon
beats.summary: At midnight Ysra and Teyo lead Pebble through the silent city.

beats.scene: Guards in blue coats search carts under hanging lanterns
beats.summary: At the Sunrise Gate guards search everyone, and the order is that the Vell girl must not leave.

beats.scene: Teyo buries a girl under blankets on a strider's back
beats.summary: Teyo hides Ysra under blankets on Pebble's back and walks to the gate, whistling.

beats.scene: A guard prods blankets with a spear while a strider stamps and bellows
beats.summary: Pebble bellows, the guard leaps back, and Teyo calms him with a handful of dates.

beats.scene: Two figures and a strider walk toward a dark desert as city lights fade
beats.summary: Beyond the gate the Sandwrights fill every skin at the Old Cistern, and the lights of Oshenar sink behind.

beats.scene: Two travellers and a tall strider walk across pale sand under thick stars
beats.summary: They travel all night under the stars, and Teyo explains that a sensible traveller walks while it is cool.

beats.scene: A girl shivers in two blankets on cold sand beside a strider
beats.summary: The desert night turns bitterly cold, because dry, clear air does not hold the day's heat.

beats.scene: Blankets stretched between two poles make shade beside a large rock
beats.summary: At dawn Teyo builds a roof of shade from two poles and the blankets, and Ysra helps.

beats.scene: A girl lies still under a blanket roof as the air shimmers outside
beats.summary: At noon the sand is too hot to touch, and Teyo teaches Ysra to lie still and save her sweat.

beats.scene: A grey cloth stretched over stones tilts toward a clay bowl in the dark
beats.summary: On the second night Teyo sets the dew-sail on a frame of stones before dawn.

beats.scene: Silver drops cover a grey cloth as a girl tastes water from a bowl
beats.summary: At sunrise the dew-sail is beaded with drops, and Ysra tastes the first cold water.

beats.scene: Teyo draws in the sand with a stick as a girl watches
beats.summary: Teyo explains that cold cloth turns the air's hidden water into drops, though only a few cups.

beats.scene: Wavy ripples in the sand run in lines toward a pale horizon
beats.summary: Teyo shows Ysra the ripples that the wind has made, steep on the sheltered side.

beats.scene: A girl crouches to trace sand ripples with her finger at night
beats.summary: Ysra practises all night and learns to read the wind's direction by herself.

beats.scene: A bright star hangs above a dark dune while a girl looks up
beats.summary: Teyo shows Ysra the Lantern Star that never moves, and she feels almost calm.

beats.scene: Two deep wheel furrows cross pale sand beneath a starry sky
beats.summary: On the fifth night Pebble stops, and two deep tracks run across the desert from horizon to horizon.

beats.scene: A girl kneels and presses her hand into a deep wheel furrow
beats.summary: Ysra measures the tracks and counts at least thirty heavy carts.

beats.scene: Teyo stands still and stares east along the tracks
beats.summary: Teyo says that carts carry water into cities and never out into the desert.

beats.scene: Two lanes of wheel tracks, one deep and one shallow, lie side by side
beats.summary: The eastward tracks are deep and the westward ones shallow, so the carts go out full.

beats.scene: Two figures crouch low among dunes as a lantern glows far ahead
beats.summary: They follow the tracks at a distance and hide twice from a passing lantern.

beats.scene: A tiny fire burns in a deep sandy hollow beside a resting strider
beats.summary: Teyo lights a small fire where no light can be seen, and they eat bread and dates.

beats.scene: Teyo speaks quietly beside a dying fire as a girl listens
beats.summary: Teyo tells Ysra the first law of the Sandwrights: water belongs to whoever needs it.

beats.scene: A girl gazes into a fire while a young man pokes the embers
beats.summary: Ysra asks what happens to a person who keeps water from the thirsty.

beats.scene: A young man with a thoughtful smile sits beside embers
beats.summary: Teyo tells Ysra about his grandmother Amma Zeri and why he became a guide.

beats.scene: A girl holds a brass cup as a young man sniffs the wind
beats.summary: Ysra tells Teyo about her father and the promise of water, and Teyo smells hot metal on the wind.

beats.scene: A huge copper-coloured cloud swallows the stars above a dark desert
beats.summary: Before dawn a wall of copper cloud rises in the east, and Teyo breaks camp in a hurry.

beats.scene: Two figures and a strider run across sand toward a ridge of black rocks
beats.summary: Teyo shouts that this is a glass storm: hot wind carrying sand that lightning has melted into glass.

beats.scene: A hollow beneath a rocky overhang is hung with blankets and wedged with stones
beats.summary: They shelter in a hollow under the rocks while Teyo ties blankets over the opening and covers Pebble's eyes.

beats.scene: Lightning flickers through a black storm as grains of glass hammer on rock
beats.summary: The storm arrives with a roar, and the dawn turns black and hot.

beats.scene: A girl whispers to a trembling strider in a cramped dark hollow
beats.summary: After an hour Pebble panics, and Ysra crawls to her head and begins to sing.

beats.scene: Two voices sing together in a rocky hollow as a strider grows calm
beats.summary: Ysra sings the old Oshenar counting rhyme, and Teyo joins her out of tune.

beats.scene: Two figures dig out of a hollow as warm sand pours in
beats.summary: After many hours the storm ends, and they dig themselves out.

beats.scene: A plain glittering with tiny green and gold glass beads
beats.summary: Outside, the whole desert glitters with beads of glass that chime underfoot.

beats.scene: Teyo and Ysra stand among new dunes that have buried every landmark
beats.summary: The dunes have moved and every landmark is gone, and Teyo jokes with worry in his eyes.

beats.scene: A girl crouches to read ripples in glittering sand as the first star appears
beats.summary: Ysra reads the ripples, finds the Lantern Star and works out which way is north.

beats.scene: A girl presses her palm on damp sand beside a slit water skin
beats.summary: A flying splinter of glass has slit one water skin, and half a day's water is lost.

beats.scene: A girl counts water skins laid in a row on glittering sand
beats.summary: Eight skins are left, enough for four days, and the nearest pool is three to five days away.

beats.scene: A girl holds a water skin as a hand closes over hers
beats.summary: On the second afternoon Ysra is desperately thirsty and wants to drink it all.

beats.scene: Teyo holds up one finger as a girl takes a tiny sip
beats.summary: Teyo teaches her to sip slowly, rest in the shade and keep quiet.

beats.scene: A tall strider with a drooping head walks beside two thirsty travellers at night
beats.summary: They walk through two long nights, and Pebble slows, though striders can endure thirst.

beats.scene: A small flock of birds flies low across a darkening sky
beats.summary: Teyo spots sandgrouse flying low at dusk toward water, and Ysra sees lichen on the rocks.

beats.scene: A narrow crack in a low cliff and a strider squeezing sideways
beats.summary: The birds lead them to a crack in a cliff and a cave with a hidden pool.

beats.scene: A tiny old woman hands a cup to a girl beside a black pool
beats.summary: Mother Sabe, keeper of the pool, gives them water and refuses payment.

beats.scene: An old woman holds up a jar of pebbles beside a lantern
beats.summary: Sabe says her pool is falling for the first time and the heavy carts go east.

beats.scene: An old woman draws a charcoal cross on a map by lantern light
beats.summary: After a day of rest Sabe marks the Stone Gate on Orla's map.

beats.scene: An old woman stands with a lantern at a crack in a cliff
beats.summary: At dusk Ysra and Teyo leave the pool with full skins, and Sabe gives Ysra dates and a warning.

beats.scene: A girl scrapes at a white salt crust under a bright moon
beats.summary: They cross a vast plain of white salt, the bed of the old sea, and Ysra finds a tiny shell.

beats.scene: A tall carved grey pillar leans half buried beside a salt plain
beats.summary: At dawn they reach a tall pillar of the Channelwrights, half buried in sand.

beats.scene: A girl runs her fingers over tiny numbers carved on a stone pillar
beats.summary: The pillar shows waves, numbers counted in hands and an arrow pointing east.

beats.scene: A girl holds an old map up against a carved pillar
beats.summary: The signs on Orla's map match the pillar, so the Silver Vein runs far beneath their feet.

beats.scene: A girl gazes at a shining blue lake on the horizon
beats.summary: At mid-morning a blue lake appears on the horizon while Teyo sleeps.

beats.scene: A girl runs across hot sand as a young man sprints after her
beats.summary: Ysra runs toward the lake, and Teyo catches her arm before she has gone far.

beats.scene: A young man holds a girl's shoulders and points at the haze
beats.summary: Teyo explains that hot air bends light, so a patch of sky looks like water.

beats.scene: A girl sits in the sand, red-faced, as a young man laughs kindly
beats.summary: Ysra is ashamed, but Teyo says that everyone runs once and he ran twice.

beats.scene: A long dark line of cliffs lies on the eastern horizon at dusk
beats.summary: At dusk they follow the pillar's arrow and see the dark line of the cliffs far ahead.

beats.scene: A wall of dark rock rises across the eastern sky over cart tracks
beats.summary: After two more nights the cliffs tower overhead, and cart tracks from the west and south converge below them.

beats.scene: Two figures and a strider lie hidden in a dry gully at dawn
beats.summary: They hide in a gully by day and hear hammers, winches and orders from beyond the ridge.

beats.scene: A huge carved stone arch barred with new iron stands in a cliff
beats.summary: From a dune at dusk Ysra and Teyo see the Stone Gate, vast and ancient and crossed with iron.

beats.scene: Tents, huts and stables stand beneath a cliff, with a blue flag above
beats.summary: A Guild camp has grown up before the gate, with guards, padlocks and a blue banner.

beats.scene: A young man hands a brass spyglass to a girl on a dune
beats.summary: Teyo lends Ysra his only treasure, a brass spyglass, and the camp springs close.

beats.scene: Barrels stand in pyramids beside a clay pond as men work winches
beats.summary: Through the glass Ysra counts hundreds of barrels, a clay pond and winch-men lifting the Vein's water.

beats.scene: A girl draws a small map in the sand beside a young man
beats.summary: Ysra counts the guards all night and finds that the north side is watched by only two men.

beats.scene: A girl peers through a spyglass at a row of huts at first light
beats.summary: At first light Ysra sees a strider with a white nose-patch tied outside the smallest hut.

beats.scene: A thin grey man in a torn coat stumbles out of a hut
beats.summary: A guard pushes a thin, grey, bearded man out of the hut, and it is Dorin.

beats.scene: A girl presses her fist to her mouth beside a comforting young man
beats.summary: Ysra weeps silently, and Teyo says that now they know where to go.

beats.scene: A girl draws a camp plan in sand while a young man studies it
beats.summary: All day in the gully Ysra and Teyo make a plan, and Ysra draws the whole camp in the sand.

beats.scene: A young man whistles on a high dune toward a distant cliff
beats.summary: Teyo explains that in cliff country a whistle bounces from rock to rock, and he can lead the guards astray.

beats.scene: A strider waits in a gully as two figures look at a camp plan
beats.summary: Ysra will free her father while Teyo draws the guards away and Pebble waits in the gully.

beats.scene: Two figures creep through broken ground toward a sleeping camp
beats.summary: After the guards change, Ysra and Teyo creep down the north side and Teyo slips away.

beats.scene: Guards run out of tents with spears and lanterns toward a far dune
beats.summary: Whistles ring from the dune, the cliffs and nowhere, and the guards run in all directions.

beats.scene: A lantern swings over sand as a girl hides behind barrels
beats.summary: A straggling guard stops near Ysra's hiding place and swings his lantern across her boot.

beats.scene: A girl lifts a heavy wooden bar from a hut door
beats.summary: Ysra reaches the smallest hut and lifts the heavy bar without a sound.

beats.scene: A thin man in a dark storeroom holds a girl's face in his hands
beats.summary: Dorin, sitting among sacks, sees Ysra at the door and takes her face in his hands.

beats.scene: Father and daughter whisper together among sacks and coils of rope
beats.summary: Dorin explains that the grey-cloaked men took him because he came too close to the Guild's secret.

beats.scene: Stane's iron-barred gate looms above a whispering father and daughter
beats.summary: Stane shut the Gate on purpose to dry up the Deep Well and store the water, to sell it back later.

beats.scene: A girl helps a thin old man across open sand toward dark shadows
beats.summary: Dorin is so weak that Ysra half carries him, and the whistling suddenly stops.

beats.scene: Torches flare around a camp as a long white-sailed skiff glides in
beats.summary: A horn blares, torches flare, and skiffs full of armed men glide across the hard ground.

beats.scene: A man in pale silk robes steps from a skiff holding a silver cane
beats.summary: Rhodric Stane steps from the first skiff, calm and clean, and says this is a pleasant surprise.

beats.scene: A smiling man in silk speaks to a girl and her father behind sacks
beats.summary: Stane offers Ysra a house with a fountain and a place in the Guild if she stays silent.

beats.scene: A girl stands tall before a ring of guards and torches
beats.summary: Ysra counts the guards, then tells Stane that water is a promise and cannot be bought.

beats.scene: A man's smile fades as guards lower their spears
beats.summary: Stane's smile slides away and he orders the guards to seize them.

beats.scene: A young man seizes a girl's hand as guards spin round
beats.summary: A whistle shrieks behind the guards, and Teyo rushes out of the dark, shouting, This way.

beats.scene: Three figures run beneath a cliff as torches bob behind them
beats.summary: The three race along a narrow cliff path with the guards' torches behind them.

beats.scene: A low green-black bronze door hides behind a fallen boulder at a cliff foot
beats.summary: Ysra remembers a door on Orla's map, and they find it behind a boulder.

beats.scene: Three figures stand in dark torchlight inside a long arched tunnel
beats.summary: They tumble inside and jam the door, and Teyo lights a torch to show a long tunnel.

beats.scene: Torchlight shows painted walls in blue, ochre and gold along a tunnel
beats.summary: In the torchlight the tunnel's walls glow with Channelwright paintings as fresh as the day they were made.

beats.scene: A great painted map of branching blue rivers covers a tunnel wall
beats.summary: The first painting is a map of rivers like veins, with one broad silver line running to Oshenar.

beats.scene: Painted rain, sand, a great gate and a wheel on a tunnel wall
beats.summary: More paintings tell the river's story: rain, sand, a great gate with a wheel, and a happy city.

beats.scene: An exhausted man leans on a painted wall as a girl studies it
beats.summary: Dorin whispers that the Channelwrights were teachers as well as builders and painted these walls for those to come.

beats.scene: A girl runs her finger down a painted table of numbers
beats.summary: Ysra finds a table of numbers, turns against hands of water, and Teyo reads, What the river gives, give on.

beats.scene: Guards' torches glow along painted walls as three figures hurry deeper
beats.summary: The bronze door gives way with a crash, and the three hurry deeper into the cliff.

beats.scene: A vast iron wheel wrapped in heavy chains fills a round chamber
beats.summary: The tunnel ends at a chamber with a vast iron wheel wrapped in chains.

beats.scene: A young man and a girl tug at chains beneath a steel padlock
beats.summary: They cannot break the chains or the lock, and the guards are coming.

beats.scene: A girl with closed eyes stands before a painting of a small wheel
beats.summary: Ysra recalls the painting in her mind and finds a second wheel drawn in its corner.

beats.scene: A young man taps stones on a wall with a torch in his hand
beats.summary: Dorin laughs, because the builders always made two ways, and Teyo begins to search the wall.

beats.scene: A young man taps stones along a wall's foot as a girl points
beats.summary: Teyo taps the stones at the foot of the wall while Ysra, guided by the painting in her mind, calls directions.

beats.scene: A stone slides from a wall to show a small green bronze wheel
beats.summary: At the eleventh stone Teyo works it loose and finds a small green bronze wheel.

beats.scene: An angry captain with a grey moustache stands in a torch-lit tunnel
beats.summary: Captain Harl shouts from the far end of the chamber, with thirty torches behind him.

beats.scene: Three figures heave on a stiff bronze wheel with a pole as a lever
beats.summary: The old wheel is stiff, so Teyo jams a pole between the spokes and the three heave together.

beats.scene: A bronze wheel turns with a groan as dust falls from a ceiling
beats.summary: With a groan the wheel gives way, and Ysra counts that eight more turns will open the drain.

beats.scene: Cold mist seeps from cracks in a wall as a man smiles in wonder
beats.summary: A roar grows behind the wall, and the chamber fills with the smell of rain.

beats.scene: A section of wall swings aside as silver water bursts into a chamber
beats.summary: On the ninth turn the wall swings aside and the Silver Vein pours in as the three climb a ledge.

beats.scene: Guards flee up a tunnel as water foams behind them in torchlight
beats.summary: The water drives the guards back up the tunnel and puts out their torches, then Teyo's.

beats.scene: Three figures cling to a stone ledge in black, roaring darkness
beats.summary: In the dark Ysra counts her heartbeats and holds her father's hand, and Dorin laughs.

beats.scene: Three figures climb stone steps toward a grey patch of dawn light
beats.summary: The flood settles into a stream, and the three climb a stair toward the light of dawn.

beats.scene: A wide silver river runs from a cliff arch straight across a golden desert
beats.summary: From a ledge on the cliff they see the Silver Vein pouring from an arch and running across the desert in its stone channel.

beats.scene: A clay pond's wall collapses and water rushes into a river as barrels spin
beats.summary: The wall of Stane's pond cracks, and all his stolen water pours back into the river.

beats.scene: Guards and workers kneel at a riverbank, cupping water in their hands
beats.summary: The guards and winch-men stare at the river, and some kneel to drink.

beats.scene: A furious man in muddy silk robes shouts at a crowd of workers
beats.summary: Stane screams at the winch-men to go into the tunnel and close what the intruders opened.

beats.scene: A grey-bearded man lowers a crank handle as others lay down tools
beats.summary: Tobin the winch-man refuses, and one by one the other men lay down their tools.

beats.scene: An officer sits on a barrel with folded arms as a man throws gold
beats.summary: Stane threatens and bribes in vain, and Captain Harl sits down on a barrel and says he cares more about his family.

beats.scene: A man in silk runs up a slope toward a white-sailed skiff
beats.summary: Stane flees in his skiff toward Oshenar to tell his own story first.

beats.scene: A dripping captain hands a thick blue-covered book to a girl
beats.summary: Captain Harl gives Ysra the camp's honest Tally Book of every barrel filled.

beats.scene: A strider nuzzles a girl as a man buries his face in another's neck
beats.summary: Teyo fetches Pebble, Dorin is reunited with his strider, and the party rides west beside the new river.

beats.scene: A girl kneels to wash her face at a river bank by a camp
beats.summary: That night Ysra washes the dust from her face and falls asleep without counting.

beats.scene: Tiny green shoots push through damp sand along a shining river
beats.summary: Along the channel the banks turn green as seeds that slept for years wake at the touch of water.

beats.scene: A tiny old woman cups a young man's face beside a river
beats.summary: Teyo's grandmother Amma Zeri leads a band of Sandwrights to see the new river and greets her grandson.

beats.scene: A sail-driven skiff glides up carrying seven waving workers
beats.summary: Tobin and six winch-men arrive on a skiff lent by Captain Harl, bringing Stane's padlock.

beats.scene: A girl turns pages of a thick book by firelight beside a quiet man
beats.summary: By firelight Ysra checks the Tally Book against the fall of the Deep Well, and the figures match.

beats.scene: A distant golden city on a plain with a silver channel running toward it
beats.summary: On the seventh day they see Oshenar and a crowd on the east wall waiting for the river.

beats.scene: A baker drops his rolling pin at a door and bursts into tears
beats.summary: Hooded and dusty, they slip into Oshenar, and Maro weeps and hides them in his bakery.

beats.scene: A girl in a nightgown leaps into another girl's arms at a back door
beats.summary: That night Pell and Granny Orla come to the bakery, and Pell has saved a cup of water for Ysra.

beats.scene: A crowd cheers around a stone well-house as an old man hauls a rope
beats.summary: Five days later the Deep Well rises, and the Rope Keeper's rope comes up wet a hand longer.

beats.scene: A man in a fresh blue robe lifts his arms before a cheering crowd
beats.summary: Stane climbs the platform and claims that his own engineers opened the Silver Vein.

beats.scene: A girl in a pulled-back hood pushes through a crowd with a thick book
beats.summary: Ysra pushes through the crowd and says, That is not true.

beats.scene: A smiling man in blue silk gestures as two guards push through a crowd
beats.summary: Stane calls Ysra a confused child, and two guards push through the crowd toward her.

beats.scene: Three people stand as a winch-man holds up a padlock
beats.summary: Dorin and Teyo stand beside Ysra, and Tobin shows the lock bearing Stane's silver seal.

beats.scene: A girl reads from a thick book before a hushed crowd
beats.summary: Ysra reads the Tally Book and shows that its figures match the fall of the rope.

beats.scene: A red-faced man flings his arms about before a silent crowd
beats.summary: Stane shouts that everything is forged, but the crowd stops cheering.

beats.scene: A tiny old woman rises from a stool with a dark stick
beats.summary: Elder Maris Thorne rises and says the Council will hear every side in the great hall.

beats.scene: People sit around a long table covered with maps and a padlock
beats.summary: For two days the Council hears Tobin, Dorin, Teyo and above all Ysra.

beats.scene: An old woman tears a document in two before a seated council
beats.summary: The Council votes to strip Stane of the silver seal, and the Elder tears up the Law of Scarcity.

beats.scene: A baker and two big sons block a thin man at a door
beats.summary: Stane is led away, and Maro and his sons catch Fennick Dray as he tries to slip out.

beats.scene: An old woman and a girl talk quietly in an empty hall
beats.summary: That night Elder Maris asks Ysra what the city should do next.

beats.scene: A girl counts three fingers before a council in a torch-lit hall
beats.summary: Ysra proposes the Open Well Law, with three rules and a river that belongs to whoever is thirsty.

beats.scene: An old woman reads a law aloud as a crowd cheers at dawn
beats.summary: At sunrise the Council passes the Open Well Law, and Elder Maris reads it aloud from Stane's platform.

beats.scene: A brass cup rests in a niche on a white stone pillar
beats.summary: The Vell family's Brass Cup becomes the city's official measure, set on a white pillar in the square.

beats.scene: A long queue of people with cups waits, a small girl first
beats.summary: On the first morning of the new law Pell is first in the queue and her chipped cup is filled.

beats.scene: A girl hands a folded grey cloth to a young man
beats.summary: Ysra pays Teyo with the finest dew-sail, and the Council asks the Sandwrights to keep the desert and the Gate.

beats.scene: A young man bows while an old woman nods in the crowd
beats.summary: Teyo accepts for his people but says he will keep wandering, and promises to whistle at the gate each spring.

beats.scene: A man sits up in bed with tea while a girl counts coins
beats.summary: Dorin recovers and gives Ysra the shop, and she chooses to be both a merchant and a keeper of the Stone Gate.

beats.scene: Palm trees, green gardens and sparkling rooftops line a stone channel
beats.summary: Gardens and palms line the channel, dew-sails hang on every roof, and Granny Orla's fountain runs free.

beats.scene: Dry brown hills beyond a green city beside a flowing channel
beats.summary: A year later a terrible drought strikes, but the Open Well Law carries the city through.

beats.scene: A girl chalks a number on a large black board beside a small girl
beats.summary: Each morning Ysra reads the rope and chalks the number, and Pell counts along.

beats.scene: A girl pockets a small brass cup on a green rooftop at dawn
beats.summary: At dawn Ysra fills her jars on the roof again, with a green city below and Teyo's whistle on the wind.

A1A2: Ysra fills her jars at dawn in the desert city.
From the roof, she can see the whole city and its well.
Ysra counts everything: fourteen stairs, twelve jars, and ten cups.
Her father opens the shop and hangs the brass cup by the door.
Maro the baker buys three cups of water for his ovens.
Dorin says, “Water is a promise, and a promise must be kept.”
Little Pell brings her old cup, and Ysra fills it gently.
At noon the market is busy, and blue Guild flags hang everywhere.
People whisper that the Deep Well is lower than before.
At dusk they look at the rope, and the water is low.
A loud bell rings, and people hurry to the market.
Guildmaster Stane steps onto the stage in rich blue robes.
He says the well is failing, and everyone must be careful.
Then he says the price of water will double.
The people shout angrily, but the blue guards stand ready.
Dorin says he will not raise his price at the shop.
Ysra does the sums, and the numbers do not fit.
A thin old woman cannot pay the Guild's new price.
Ysra sees Stane's green garden through a gap in the wall.
At night, carts full of barrels roll out of the garden.
Ysra runs home and tells her father everything she saw.
Dorin shows an old map with a thin silver line.
Dorin says a river runs deep under the sand.
Long ago, builders made channels to guide the water.
If the river is blocked, the well will run dry.
Ysra says, “I will come too,” but he says no.
Dorin buys four water skins and hires two drivers.
At the gate, Dorin hugs Ysra and gives her the cup.
The caravan walks out as the sun comes up.
Ysra walks home alone and opens the shop herself.
Ysra opens the shop every day and marks the wall.
Money is short, but Ysra keeps her father's fair price.
On day eight, Pell asks, “Is your father back yet?”
On day ten, Ysra waits at the gate until dark.
Twelve days pass, then fifteen, and the road stays empty.
One evening, Bastian the driver comes back alone and very tired.
Bastian says armed men stopped them and took Dorin away.
Ysra asks the Guild for help, but they only shrug.
A thin man in a grey coat visits the shop.
Ysra shares her last jar and decides to find her father.
Ysra asks every caravan master, but none will go.
Old Granny Orla sells water beside a small fountain.
Orla listens and then takes Ysra into her house.
Orla gives her a map drawn long ago by hand.
Orla warns that the Glass Desert is full of danger.
Orla says the Sandwrights camp outside the east wall.
At noon Ysra walks out to the camp of the Sandwrights.
A young man in a blue robe watches a ribbon on a pole.
Ysra asks him to guide her, but Teyo says no.
Teyo agrees to guide her for a fine cloth from her father's shop.
Ysra takes a grey cloth from her father's best chest.
Pebble is a tall, calm animal with kind brown eyes.
Teyo shows her how much water to carry each day.
Ysra counts the skins, and the numbers all agree.
Ysra gives Maro the shop key and says goodbye.
Under a thin moon, Ysra and Teyo lead Pebble through the streets.
At the gate, guards are looking for a girl named Ysra.
Teyo hides Ysra under a cloth on Pebble's back.
A guard pokes the blankets, and Pebble stamps her foot.
Beyond the gate, Ysra sits up and sees the dark desert.
They walk all night under a sky full of stars.
The desert night is cold, so they wear warm blankets.
At dawn they stop and make a shelter from blankets.
In the heat of the day, they lie still and rest.
Before the second dawn, Teyo spreads the dew-sail on stones.
At sunrise, drops of water shine on the cloth.
Teyo says the cold cloth turns hidden water in the air into drops.
Teyo points to wavy lines in the sand.
Ysra reads the ripples and finds the way herself.
Ysra finds the Lantern Star, which never moves.
On the fifth night, they find deep wheel tracks in the sand.
Ysra bends down and studies the tracks with great care.
Teyo says carts bring water into cities, not out.
Ysra sees that the tracks are deeper going east.
They follow the tracks, but they keep far away.
That night they light a tiny fire in a hollow.
Teyo says the Sandwrights share water with whoever needs it.
Ysra asks about a man who keeps all the water.
Teyo says his grandmother taught him to read the desert.
Ysra tells her story, but Teyo smells something in the wind.
The sky turns copper, and Teyo says they must hurry.
They run to the rocks, and Teyo explains the storm.
They find a hollow in the rocks and hide inside.
The storm arrives with a roar, and the day turns dark.
Pebble is afraid, but Ysra sings to her softly.
The song is a counting rhyme, and Teyo sings too.
At last the roar stops, and everything is quiet.
Outside, the whole desert shines with tiny glass beads.
The dunes have moved, and every landmark is gone.
Ysra reads the ripples and finds the way north.
The storm cut a water skin, and water is lost.
Ysra counts the skins: eight are left, and the road is long.
Ysra is very thirsty, and she wants to drink everything.
Teyo says, “Drink a little at a time,” and shows her.
They walk through the night, and Pebble gets slow.
At dusk they see birds flying low in one direction.
In a crack in the rocks, they find a hidden pool.
The old keeper says, “Drink,” and asks for nothing.
Sabe says the pool is getting lower every month.
Sabe draws a mark on the map to show the Stone Gate.
Ysra and Teyo thank Sabe and leave the pool at dusk.
Next they cross a flat white plain that was once a sea.
At dawn they see a tall stone pillar in the sand.
The pillar shows waves, numbers, and an arrow pointing east.
The same signs are on Orla's map, so the river is near.
In the morning heat, Ysra sees a lake far away.
Ysra runs toward the water, but Teyo catches her arm.
Teyo says hot air bends the light and makes a false lake.
Ysra feels silly, but Teyo says everyone runs once.
At dusk they see a dark line of cliffs far to the east.
For two nights they walk toward the cliffs, and the cliffs grow.
At dawn they hide in a dry valley and listen.
From a dune, they see a huge stone gate in the cliff.
Below the gate, there are tents, huts and many guards.
Teyo has a small brass spyglass, and Ysra looks first.
She sees barrels, a big pond, and men pulling ropes.
Ysra counts the guards and sees when they change places.
At sunrise, Ysra sees her father's riding animal tied outside a hut.
Then the door opens, and her father comes out.
Ysra covers her mouth, and Teyo says, “Now we know.”
All day they plan, and Ysra draws a map in the sand.
Teyo says his whistles can sound like they come from anywhere.
Ysra will go for her father, and Pebble will wait.
At midnight, they creep down the ridge in the dark.
From a far dune, a loud whistle cuts through the night.
A guard runs past, and Ysra hides behind the barrels.
Ysra finds the small hut and lifts the heavy bar.
Inside, her father looks up, and she runs to him.
Dorin says men in grey cloaks took him on the road.
Stane closed the Stone Gate, and he keeps the water.
Dorin is weak, so Ysra helps him out of the hut.
A horn sounds, and a big sail comes across the sand.
Out steps Guildmaster Stane, in fine robes, and he smiles.
Stane knows her name, and he smiles like a friend.
Ysra counts the cost, and she says no.
Stane stops smiling and tells his guards to take them.
Suddenly a sharp whistle sounds behind the guards.
They run along the cliff path, and the guards chase them.
Teyo finds a small door in the rock and pulls it open.
They run inside, and Teyo lights a torch in the dark.
Inside the tunnel, the walls are covered with old paintings.
The first painting is a map of rivers like veins.
The next paintings show rain, a river, a gate, and a city.
Dorin says the builders painted the walls to teach later people.
Ysra studies a table of numbers beside the wheel picture.
Behind them, the guards break the bronze door with a loud crash.
At the end, they find a huge iron wheel wrapped in chains.
They pull at the chains, but the lock will not open.
Ysra remembers the painting and sees a second small wheel.
Dorin says the old builders always made two ways.
Teyo taps the wall stone by stone, and one sounds hollow.
Behind the loose stone, there is a small green wheel.
Captain Harl shouts, “Stop, in the Guildmaster's name!”
Teyo, Ysra and Dorin push the stiff wheel together.
At last the old wheel moves and starts to turn.
Behind the wall, they hear water rushing in the dark.
The last turn comes, and the wall opens to the water.
The guards run back, and their torches go out.
In the dark, Ysra counts her heartbeats and holds her father's hand.
At last the roar gets softer, and grey light shows above them.
From the cliff, they see a wide silver river in the desert.
Stane's big clay pond breaks, and its water joins the river.
The guards and workers stand and stare at the river.
Stane runs out of his tent and shouts, “Close the gate again!”
The workers say, “We will not, because we are thirsty too.”
Stane shouts and begs, but nobody listens to him.
Stane runs to his skiff and sails away toward the city.
Captain Harl gives Ysra the camp's book of numbers.
Teyo brings Pebble and Dorin's strider, and they leave.
That night, Ysra washes her face in the river and smiles.
Along the river, tiny green shoots push up through the sand.
Teyo's grandmother, Amma Zeri, comes to see the new river.
Tobin and six workers come by skiff with Stane's steel lock.
By the fire, Ysra checks the Guild's numbers with her own.
From a dune, they see Oshenar and its shining new river.
They enter the city quietly, and Maro cries when he sees her.
Pell hugs Ysra, and Granny Orla cries with joy.
Five days later, the Deep Well begins to rise.
Then Stane climbs up and says he saved the city.
Ysra steps out of the crowd and says, “That is not true.”
Stane smiles, but the guards move toward Ysra.
Dorin and Teyo stand beside her, and Tobin steps forward.
Ysra opens the tally book and reads out the numbers.
Stane says it is all lies, but the people look worried.
Elder Maris Thorne stands and calls the council to hear the truth.
For two days, the Council hears all the proof.
The Council votes to take away Stane's silver seal.
Guards lead Stane away, and thin Fennick Dray is caught too.
The Elder asks Ysra what should happen to the well now.
Ysra says the well must be measured in public and shared fairly.
At sunrise, the Council votes yes, and the Open Well Law begins.
The Vell family's brass cup becomes the city's measure.
Pell stands first in the line with her chipped cup.
Ysra gives Teyo the dew-sail she promised him.
Teyo says yes for his people, but he will keep walking.
Dorin gets strong, and Ysra chooses to be a merchant and a keeper.
Along the channel, the city plants palm trees and gardens.
A year later, a drought comes, but the city is safe.
Ysra reads the rope each morning, and the cup is always fair.
At dawn Ysra fills her jars on the roof again.
B1B2: Ysra Vell fills her clay jars on the roof as the sun rises over Oshenar. In the middle of the city lies the Deep Well, and everyone depends on it.
From the roof, Ysra can see every street of Oshenar, with its flat roofs and blue tiles. All the streets lead to the round stone Well-House in the middle.
Ysra has always counted things, because numbers make her feel calm. She knows there are fourteen stairs to the roof, twelve jars on the shelf and nine hundred steps to the well.
Downstairs, Dorin Vell is already opening the shutters of the family shop. On a hook beside the door hangs the old brass cup that measures every sale.
Maro the baker comes first, as he does every morning, and asks for three cups. Dorin fills the brass cup to the very brim, never a drop more or less.
When Maro has gone, Ysra asks why her father is so careful with every single drop. Dorin smiles and says that water is a promise, and a promise is only worth something if it is always the same.
Little Pell from next door comes to the shop with a chipped clay cup. Ysra fills it to the top, and Pell asks why the desert has to be so big.
At noon the market square is full of shade-cloths, spice sellers and noise. Above every stall hangs the blue banner of the Well-Guild, which controls most of the city's water.
Near the fruit stalls, Ysra hears people whispering that the Deep Well has fallen. The queue at the Well-House is longer than she has ever seen it.

At dusk Ysra and her father walk to the Well-House, where the old Rope Keeper lets them look at the rope. The marks show that the water is three hands lower than last month, which is the lowest it has ever been.
The next morning a bell rings from the tower of the Guild Hall, and the shops empty into the square. Ysra and Dorin push through the crowd to hear what the Guildmaster has to say.
Rhodric Stane, the Guildmaster, climbs onto the platform in robes of deep blue silk. He wears silver rings on every finger, and his voice is as smooth as oil.
Stane tells the crowd that the Deep Well is failing and that the desert has grown angry. The Guild, he promises, will protect every citizen, but everyone must make sacrifices.
Then, with a sad smile, Stane announces that from tomorrow the price of every cup of water will be doubled. He says it is the only way to make the water last for everyone.
The crowd shouts with anger and fear, but a line of guards in blue coats steps forward to keep order. Stane waves one ringed hand and says that nobody should blame the Guild for the weather.
Back at the shop, Dorin says quietly that he will not double his price. Ysra opens the ledger and begins to work out what that will cost them.
That night Ysra studies the numbers and frowns, because they do not add up. The well has fallen three hands in one month, yet the city has not used any more water than usual.
The next day an old seamstress comes to the shop, because she cannot afford the Guild's new price. Dorin fills her jug at the old price, and Ysra writes the sale down with a worried frown.
At dusk Ysra carries two jars up to the high district, where the richest families live. Through a gap in a wall she sees a green garden of palms and fountains, under the Guildmaster's silver seal.
Later, hiding in the shadows, Ysra watches the garden gate swing open. Heavy carts roll out, and she can hear water slopping inside the barrels.
Ysra runs home and tells her father about the garden and the secret carts. Dorin listens without a word, and then he goes slowly to the old chest under the stairs.
From the chest Dorin takes a cracked old map and spreads it across the counter. A thin silver line runs across it, far below the great yellow desert.

This is the Silver Vein, Dorin says, a hidden river that moves slowly through the sand and rock deep under the desert. Rain fell on far mountains long ago, and the water has been creeping towards Oshenar ever since.

Dorin says that long ago the Channelwrights, the great builders, dug channels to guide the Vein towards the city. His grandfather used to talk about a huge stone gate in the cliffs that controlled the flow.
If something is blocking the Vein, Dorin says, the Deep Well will keep falling until it is empty. He must go to the Cold Springs, where the river rises, to find out the truth.
Ysra says she wants to come too, but Dorin shakes his head. Someone has to keep the shop open, he says, and nobody is better with numbers than his daughter.
Over the next two days Dorin hires two drivers, including a cheerful man named Bastian, and loads four striders with water skins. Ysra counts everything twice, and the total is just enough.
At the Sunrise Gate, Dorin hugs his daughter and presses the brass cup into her hands. If he is not back in ten days, he says, she must not follow him.
The tall striders file out through the gate, with the rising sun behind them. Ysra watches until the last one is a dark speck in the pale dust.
Ysra walks home with the brass cup tight in her fist, and for the first time she opens the shop alone. She hangs the cup on its hook, takes a deep breath and counts the first day.
Day after day Ysra opens the shop, measures the water and marks the wall with chalk. Maro the baker brings a warm loaf every morning and asks how she is.
The Guild now charges the shop double for every barrel, so each sale loses a little money. Ysra still sells at her father's price, and she makes up the difference by eating less.

On the eighth day little Pell stands at the counter with her chipped cup and asks whether Ysra's father is back yet. Ysra says soon, and the word tastes strange in her mouth because she does not know if it is true.
On the tenth day, the day her father promised, Ysra goes to the Sunrise Gate and waits there until the sun sets. The road stays empty, and the guards at last tell her to go home.
Twelve days pass, and then fifteen, and still the road beyond the gate is empty. Ysra stops sleeping well, and in the night she listens for footsteps that never come.
On the evening of the fifteenth day, Bastian the driver staggers through the gate on foot. He is sunburnt and thin, and he has no strider, no baggage and no hat.
Between sips of water, Bastian says that armed men stopped the caravan on the eastern road. They took Dorin and the other driver away, and sent Bastian home on foot with a warning.
The next morning Ysra goes to the Guild Hall and asks for help in finding her father. A polite clerk writes her name in a book and says that accidents happen in the desert.
That afternoon a thin man in a grey coat, Fennick Dray, offers to buy the Vell shop for a tiny sum. Ysra says that the shop is not for sale, and he leaves with a cold smile and a warning.
That night Ysra shares the last full jar with her thirsty neighbours, and the shelves are empty. As she sweeps the floor she makes up her mind: if nobody will find her father, she will do it herself.
The next morning Ysra visits every caravan master in Oshenar and asks for a guide. They all shake their heads, because the Glass Desert has swallowed too many travellers.

On a dusty corner, old Granny Orla sells water from a clay jar beside a tiny fountain that has almost stopped. She has known Ysra since the girl was small, and she takes one look at her face and puts down her ladle.

Orla listens to the whole story without speaking, and then she locks her cart and leads Ysra into the back room. There she kneels beside her bed and pulls out a flat wooden box tied with a faded red cord.
Inside the box is a hand-drawn map of the Silver Vein, with a thin silver line and many small marks. Orla says that her grandmother copied it long ago from a chest belonging to the Channelwrights.
Orla warns Ysra that the Glass Desert is full of dangers: hot storms, false lakes and sand that moves. A girl who goes alone, she says, will be lost before the second sunset.
The Sandwrights, Orla says, are the people who read the desert, and they camp beside the Old Cistern outside the east wall. She tells Ysra to ask there for a young man who whistles.
At noon Ysra slips through the Sunrise Gate and walks to the Old Cistern, where grey tents stand in a circle. A woman gives her a cup of water before she has said a single word.

At midnight, under a thin moon, Ysra and Teyo lead Pebble through the silent streets, with the folded skins on her back. Every footstep seems very loud to Ysra, and every dark doorway seems to hide a guard.

From the last street, Ysra and Teyo watch a dozen guards in blue coats searching every cart and every traveller at the Sunrise Gate. A sergeant tells a pedlar that nobody may carry water out of Oshenar, and that the daughter of Dorin Vell must not leave.
Teyo pushes Ysra up onto Pebble's back and covers her with a heap of blankets and folded skins. Then he walks to the gate, calm as a man going to market.

A guard asks where Teyo is going, and he says that his strider wants a night walk. The guard pokes the blankets with his spear, but Pebble stamps and snorts, and Teyo offers the man a handful of sweet dates.

Beyond the gate Teyo lifts the blankets, and Ysra sits up, laughing and shaking. At the Old Cistern the Sandwrights fill every skin without asking for a coin, and the lights of Oshenar sink behind them.

Outside, the sun is shining on a world covered in tiny glass beads, green and gold and clear as water. They crunch and chime under Ysra's boots like thousands of little bells.

By the second afternoon Ysra's lips are cracked and her tongue feels like old leather. She holds a skin in both hands and wants, more than anything, to drink it all.
